goal_status: Active. Official competition performance and SOTA are not established.
scope: Standalone research on the authorized erdos-3242 lab host. No production farm, SkyPilot holder job, or controller changes. No GCS transfers.

literature.lesson: The organizer benchmark distinguishes parameter inference from OOD detection and supplies physical-summary, CNN and autoencoder baselines. Predicting cosmology accurately does not by itself establish OOD sensitivity.
literature.application: Retain complementary representations and use the specified low-FPR metric; do not compare our synthetic scores directly with its public-test results.

literature.lesson: Continuous field-level flows outperform several feature methods in a simplified weak-lensing bias-detection study. The field models are unconditional across cosmologies; the main test uses fiducial cosmology, and compressed methods receive idealized true-cosmology conditioning.
literature.application: Keep the existing masked field-flow branch as an independent source of information. Our model and data setting are not a reproduction.

literature.lesson: Flow models can reproduce summary means and variances while misestimating correlations; noisy training and augmentation can improve covariance recovery.
literature.application: Controlled four-view noise ablation: preserve normalization, architecture and validation inputs, change only training-noise coverage; then separately examine a longer training budget.

literature.lesson: Minkowski functionals contain information beyond two-point summaries in HSC weak-lensing parameter inference.
literature.application: Test fixed-mask digital morphology at three scales. These descriptors are not an unbiased continuum Minkowski estimator, and the paper does not establish their OOD performance here.

literature.lesson: Scale-conditioned learned summaries and density models expose simulator mismatch, while degeneracies can hide misspecification in a limited representation.
literature.application: Test information absent from global summaries, including regional consistency at multiple smoothing scales.

literature.lesson: Goodness-of-fit, physical data splits and closure tests diagnose different aspects of model misspecification; passing one does not establish the mechanism is correct.
literature.application: Separate normal false-positive checks, synthetic sensitivity and new-pattern closure checks; retain explicit unknowns about hidden competition physics.

training.spatial_features: 45 digital morphology and 48 regional descriptors; original 72 summaries retained unchanged.
training.first_round: Three 88-dimensional variants, each with three initialization seeds and 10000 updates: 16 morphology PCs, 16 regional PCs, or 8 of each; PCA uses training data only.
training.noise_ablation: Three 72-dimensional models trained for 10000 updates on four noise views of the same 16160 clean training realizations. Three additional noise seeds are 9301, 9302 and 9303. Normalization is bit-for-bit identical to the original one-view flow for all three seeds.
training.longer_training: Three further four-view models, 30000 updates. All three beat their 10000-update counterparts on normal validation NLL; selected checkpoints are 27500, 25000 and 26750. Selection uses normal validation NLL, not synthetic OOD scores.
training.caveat: Repeated noise views are not new independent cosmological simulations. Likelihoods of different feature spaces must not be compared numerically.

findings: Appending morphology did not improve the general detector in this implementation. Regional PCs helped spatial modulation but weakened other families.

Noise augmentation improved normal likelihood in every seed, and improved peak/IAAFT diagnostics, but reduced sensitivity to mild low-frequency smoothing. Better normal likelihood is not a universal OOD improvement.

Predicting regional descriptors from the original 72 summaries exposes additional spatial information. Its residual Mahalanobis statistic improved the strong spatial-modulation score from 0.104 for the appended-feature model to 0.307.

Centering log regional-residual scores using a normal-only regression on global summaries improved that spatial score to 0.703. Extra conditional variance scaling did not improve it. The regression is a heuristic score correction, not an exact likelihood ratio or guaranteed conditional p-value.

A frozen fresh-noise/new-pattern check supported the regional finding: 0.710 on the original sine with fresh noise, 0.675 with random phase, 0.399 at twice the spatial frequency and 0.525 for a linear gradient. It flagged 10/1024 normal maps at the nominal 1% threshold.

The corrected specialist remains weak on spectral/peak shifts. A maximum with the normal-scaled hybrid preserves much of the hybrid's sensitivity while improving the spatial-modulation diagnostic, at a measurable cost on some other families.

regional_fitting.features: 48 regional descriptors conditioned on the original 72 summaries via robust-transform ridge regression.
regional_fitting.mean_fit: 16160 training maps; alpha selected by five folds grouped by cosmology.
regional_fitting.residual_covariance: 3232 normal validation maps; fixed 10% diagonal shrinkage.
regional_fitting.score_centering: Regress log residual Mahalanobis score on the original summaries using the 3232 normal validation maps. Alpha selected by five cosmology-grouped folds. This CV is conditional on the already fitted residual model/covariance, not a cross-validation of the entire pipeline.
regional_fitting.calibration: Normal calibration medians and 90th percentiles define fixed ensemble scales. No public test samples fit any transform or model.

proposed_candidates.06: Noise-trained three-seed summary ensemble plus the unchanged two-model field branch, equal normal-scaled average.
proposed_candidates.07: Maximum of normal-scaled candidate 06 and the normal-centered regional specialist.
proposed_candidates.reason_to_keep_both: Their difference isolates the additional spatial specialist. Neither has an official leaderboard score recorded.
proposed_candidates.originals: Candidates 04 and 05 remain frozen and unchanged.

remaining_uncertainties: Official public/private OOD performance remains unknown; no official submission was made in this round.

Synthetic diagnostics and clean audit realizations have been reused. New modulation patterns use fresh noise, but do not create independent simulator realizations or recover unknown physical alternatives.
Global normal thresholds are not uniform across all physical-parameter bins; the low-Omega_m tail merits investigation.
The minimum-energy summary score profiles over a discrete nonuniform 101-cosmology grid. Whether continuous supported profiling improves conditional coverage is an untested hypothesis.
A normal-only float16 roundtrip audit on 128 maps showed median/max absolute original-summary score changes of 0.1502/0.8990. This is not a full tail-equivalence proof.
Exact private-evaluation interface, clean-environment installation and CPU numerical equivalence are not validated by the TPU checks.
next_research: Use actual leaderboard feedback to compare the frozen complementary hypotheses; do not infer real performance from the synthetic metric.
Audit the discrete cosmology profiling hypothesis using normal coverage and constrained continuous inference, with all network weights frozen.
Explore multiscale regional consistency and noise-invariant learned representations only with frozen closure tests and reported regressions.
Preserve the normal-only pointwise inference contract and avoid fitting or ranking across public test samples.

packaged_artifacts.checked: Finite scores and ZIP schema; staged frozen-bundle raw API; singleton/reverse/chunk/unobserved-NaN invariance; empty/nonfinite guards; standalone CLI.
packaged_artifacts.public_test_usage: Frozen independent inference only. Existing verified field scores reused to avoid repeated field inference.
